truths.CP2:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ol.order_id)
FROM order_lines AS ol
JOIN orders AS o ON o.order_id = ol.order_id
JOIN products AS p ON p.product_id = ol.product_id
JOIN categories AS c ON c.category_id = p.category_id
WHERE c.category_name IN ('TVs up to 43 inch', 'TVs 50-55 inch', 'TVs 65 inch and up')
  AND o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00'
  AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
truths.CP4:
WITH tv_orders AS (
  -- one row per 2025 order with a TV line
  SELECT DISTINCT ol.order_id
  FROM order_lines AS ol
  JOIN orders AS o ON o.order_id = ol.order_id
  JOIN products AS p ON p.product_id = ol.product_id
  JOIN categories AS c ON c.category_id = p.category_id
  WHERE c.category_name IN ('TVs up to 43 inch', 'TVs 50-55 inch', 'TVs 65 inch and up')
    AND o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00'
    AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
)
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (
         SELECT 1
         FROM order_lines AS sl
         JOIN products AS sp ON sp.product_id = sl.product_id
         JOIN categories AS sc ON sc.category_id = sp.category_id
         WHERE sl.order_id = t.order_id
           AND sc.category_name = 'Soundbars'
       ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2)
FROM tv_orders AS t

CP1.explanation: One row per TV order with its promotion flag counts every order once, and EXISTS only asks whether that order holds a soundbar; flagging each TV line counts an order with two TVs twice.

CP5.explanation: The result shows promoted TV orders and soundbars go together, but promotion shoppers and weeks differ from normal ones, so it cannot show cause; saying the promotion pays for itself also ignores the margin given away.
